description: The dataset of OKR Setter: the limits of the form and each rule its checks apply, with its source. The sources' addresses are in src/model.js. The examples are written for this page.

rules.text: An objective is significant, concrete, action-oriented and, ideally, inspirational. The page checks that it has a title.
An objective is not upkeep such as "keep hiring" or "maintain market position". The page flags the words keep, maintain and continue.
An objective has 3 to 5 key results.
A key result is specific, time-bound, and measurable and verifiable. The page checks that a number has a unit and a target that differs from its start, and that a score lies between 0.0 and 1.0.
A key result describes an outcome, not an activity. The page flags the words consult, help, analyze and participate.
A key result is time-bound. The page checks for a real due date.
Score a key result from 0.0 to 1.0. The sweet spot for OKRs is 60 to 70 percent.
A committed OKR is expected to score 1.0. An aspirational OKR is expected to average 0.7. Mark which one each objective is.
Common mistakes include failing to tell committed from aspirational OKRs, and key results that do not add up to the objective. A page cannot test these: read them.
